by Mike Taylor https://every.?ev_audience=free

Midjourney/Every illustration.

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up https://every.?ev_audience=free to get it in your inbox.



----------------------------------------



“Don’t freak out, I cloned you.”

That’s what I told Natalia Quintero https://every.?ev_audience=free, my boss at the time, after I distilled a year of her Slack messages into a file called natalia.md and used it to simulate whether she’d sign off on an email I was about to send a client. She didn’t freak out—in fact, she said it was her favorite call of the day.

I had just started in a consulting role reporting to Natalia, and I was worried I didn’t know how to communicate with corporate clients. Our clients were large enterprises, but I had only ever had experience working with startups. Natalia, meanwhile, had years of corporate and banking experience. I knew my tendency to write emails like I write tweets https://every.?ev_audience=free might not be professional enough for this context, but I didn’t want to be asking Natalia to check my emails multiple times a day. She had better things to do, and when she did give me advice, she was often repeating herself.

----------
howdy, it’s Barsee again.

happy friday, AI family, and welcome back to AI Valley.

**here are the biggest things worth knowing today:**

* Claude can now build live dashboards and animated videos

* AI companies are quietly preparing for a major AI disaster

* Three fired OpenAI researchers are pushing back

* Plus trending AI tools, posts, and resources

Let’s _dive_ into the Valley of AI…


----------

----------
#### **SPONSORED**

## [The Future Vision XPRIZE has a winner. Now you can invest in the film](https://republic.com/xprize)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/caebd2b7-9527-48e9-8163-63e174dbfb77/gifted__1_.jpg?t=1791545950)
Caption: Courtesy: Republic

On September 25, in front of a live audience in downtown Los Angeles, _The Gifted_ won the Future Vision XPRIZE, the world's largest sci-fi competition to imagine more positive visions of the future.

The story: an eleven-year-old genius rebuilds his dead mother as an AI. She starts guiding strangers to save lives, and the government decides her kindness is the greatest threat it has ever faced.

Now it's moving toward production with Range Media Partners, the studio behind A Complete Unknown and Longlegs.

You don't have to just watch it happen. The film is open to investors on Republic, giving you a chance to back the award-winning project before it reaches the screen.

[See the film and invest →](https://republic.com/xprize)


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

Youtube: Introducing Claude Dashboards and Claude Motion (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=en0GuyhieQk)

**1/ Claude can now build live dashboards and animated videos. **Two new things: [Claude Dashboards](https://x.com/claudeai/status/2108271552991252810?s=20) and [Claude Motion](https://claude.com/resources/articles/dashboards-and-motion).

Dashboards connects to company data (Salesforce, Snowflake and the rest) and builds charts that actually update when the numbers change. 

Motion takes reports, charts or just ideas and turns them into animated explainers. The clever bit is it uses code instead of AI video, so the text, numbers and animations stay editable. There’s also a [Send to Adobe](https://www.adobe.com/products/firefly/features/ai-video-editor.html) option so you can keep going in Firefly Video Editor. [Adobe’s Claude plugin](https://www.adobe.com/adobe-connectors/adobe-for-claude.html) already brings 80+ tools from Photoshop, Premiere, Acrobat etc into Claude, so the two are clearly getting friendlier.

Dashboards is in beta for paid users. Motion is Team and Enterprise only for now. Claude Docs, Slides and Design just came out of beta and are available on Free plans too.

Interesting timing with OpenAI’s [Intelligent UI](https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-for-everyone/) launch. Both companies are pushing past pure text, but Anthropic still feels more focused on the tools people actually use day-to-day. I’ll be trying Dashboards as soon as I get access; live updating charts from real company data is something I’ve wanted for a while.

**2/ AI companies are quietly preparing for a major AI disaster. **[Axios reported](https://www.axios.com/2026/10/09/ai-companies-day-after-major-attack) that executives at OpenAI, Anthropic and other labs are privately war-gaming a public and political backlash after a catastrophic incident — possibly as soon as 2027. Some insiders apparently expect something within the next 6–12 months. The main fear is an AI-powered cyberattack that knocks out banks, internet, electricity or water.

OpenAI confirmed they run preparedness exercises but stressed these scenarios aren’t inevitable. Anthropic declined to comment.

Worth keeping in perspective: these are scenarios being discussed, not evidence that something is about to happen. Still, the fact that the people building the stuff are running these drills says something.

**3/ Three fired OpenAI researchers are pushing back. **[Tomek Korbak, Jasmine Wang and Mikita Balesni](https://x.com/balesni/status/2108262814003687745) were let go for allegedly mishandling sensitive information. They’ve published an open letter disputing the accusations and saying OpenAI’s shifting internal rules are making people afraid to speak up.

They claim their actions were within policy (including outside research and access to an executive’s email for recruiting). Wang says she accidentally opened a sensitive email and reported it within minutes. They also deny leaking anything about models becoming harder to monitor.

OpenAI told TechCrunch the firings involved a “pattern of misconduct” and weren’t retaliation for raising safety concerns. The researchers are also worried the firings could undermine plans to bring independent auditors inside the company. OpenAI says it agrees with their recommendations, but whether those plans actually move forward is another question.


----------

----------
# TRENDING TOOLS


--------------------
* [Claude Dashboards and Claude Motion](https://x.com/claudeai/status/2108271552991252810?s=20) - ask Claude to turn your data into live dashboards and your ideas into animated explainers

* [Interface](https://x.com/carloAI/status/2108226291107602580?s=20) - the primary hardware for the agent era. It lets you control all your agents from your hand

* [REA](https://x.com/MatthewBerman/status/2108245653843509415?s=20) - one MCP for reverse engineering across applications and runtime behavior

* [Voyager](https://x.com/anvisha/status/2108252061209088159?s=20) - the open harness for S-tier video, graphics, and games

* [Odyssey-3](https://x.com/odysseyml/status/2108238378751967385?s=20) - most powerful foundation world model yet. A new state-of-the-art in Physics-IQ, and powers robots, trains AIs, and generates interactive experiences

* [Anthropic OSS Scanner](https://www.anthropic.com/research/launching-opt-in-vuln-finding-service-for-open-source?utm_source=www.theneurondaily.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=claude-dashboards-motion-launched) scans enrolled open-source projects for vulnerabilities and suggests fixes

* [Fo](https://wajo.ai/join-wajo) - a personal AI that hires humans for the tasks AI can’t do yet

* [GoodVibes](https://goodvibes.tools/) - filter X, Reddit and YouTube by vibes, in plain English. Runs on Jev

Generic AI gives everyone the same intelligence. Your Sentience is a high-fidelity digital twin shaped by your memories, relationships, voice, and judgment.

Your Sentience connects the context across your email, calendar, messages, meetings, and documents. It uses that context to prepare you for decisions, write responses you would actually send, and act with your approval. It learns from every correction and continually improves.

Your AI should become more like you, not make you more like everyone else.

Create your Sentience with code VALLEY and get one month of Sentience Max free.

[Claim your free month](https://sentience.com/download?ref=VALLEY)

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

Tweet:  (https://twitter.com/OpenAI/status/2107894997538525580?s=20)

**OpenAI rolls out GPT-6 with Intelligent UI in ChatGPT -** its new “[Intelligent UI](https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-for-everyone/)” lets ChatGPT generate interactive diagrams, calculators, charts, and other custom interfaces instead of just giving you a wall of text.

So you could ask it to plan dinner for 10 people and get a shopping list that updates as you change the guest count, or ask how much rent you can afford and get a calculator with sliders you can play with. You can even explore anatomy diagrams by clicking on different body parts.

The feature [comes with GPT-6](https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-for-everyone/), which is also making ChatGPT faster at responding. OpenAI says GPT-6 Instant starts answering web-search questions 44% sooner than GPT-5.6 Instant. Paid users got access yesterday, with Free and Go users starting to get it today.

Now, Google and Claude have been doing similar things for a while, so the idea isn't exactly new. But ChatGPT has 1.2 billion weekly users, and bringing this to free users is a pretty big deal.

btw here are some cool [use-cases](https://x.com/lucas__crespo/status/2107947574632067225?s=20) unlocked by ChatGPT's intelligent UI.

Other new AI headlines worth knowing:

**1/ **[**Claude Haiku 5.5**](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-haiku-5-5)** is cheap, until you need more context.** Anthropic's new fast model costs $0.10/$0.50 per million input/output tokens for prompts under 100K tokens, but prices jump 5x beyond that. It's priced the same as GPT-6 Luna below 100K tokens and reports better benchmark scores, though Luna looks like the better deal for longer prompts. Simon Willison has a [good breakdown](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Oct/7/claude-haiku-5-5/).

**2/ Google launches an AI game builder called Playground.** The new [no-code platform](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/ai/playground-experimental-gaming-platform/) lets you create games just by describing what you want, using Gemini, Nano Banana and Lyria. It's available to U.S. users aged 18+. Google also separately launched a [SynthID Detector](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/07/googles-new-synthid-website-can-identify-ai-generated-media/) that can identify AI-generated content across 20 file formats.

**3/ Zuckerberg wants AI to simulate human cells.** Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan's [Biohub](https://biohub.org/news/virtual-biology-initiative-expansion/) is expanding its $500M biology initiative into a $1.8B effort with the US government, Google DeepMind and Meta. The goal is a “universal virtual cell” that can predict how cells respond to drugs and other changes before scientists test them in a lab. Researchers say they'll need data from trillions of cells to make it work, compared with hundreds of millions in today's largest datasets.


----------

----------
# TRENDING TOOLS


--------------------
* [Grok Bot](https://x.com/bot/status/2107949161878606089?s=20) - can now search, read, and monitor X

* [Google Playground](https://x.com/GoogleLabs/status/2107800195748737042?s=20) - an experimental gaming platform that lets you create your own games with zero coding experience

* [Tab](https://tab.bot/) - an AI you text when you need something done

* [Google SynthID](https://synthid.com/) - lets anyone verify whether a piece of media, be it an image, a video, or an audio clip, is generated using AI

* [Claude Haiku 5.5](https://x.com/claudeai/status/2107894039626277339) - cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model released

Caption: Sam Altman. Photo: Heather Diehl/Getty Images

**OpenAI releases internal model’s findings on 377 math problems **- they give an internal model ~4000 open research problems and get [722 manuscripts](https://openai.com/index/sharing-ai-progress-in-mathematics/) proving 372 families of new results in number theory, theoretical computer science, physics, etc.

They claim to prove a "quasi-Riemann hypothesis", which while not the $1M Riemann Hypothesis from the Millennium Prize problems, is not far from it. For 162 of the manuscripts, they formalize the main result in Lean, which is then mechanically verified by a computer.

Most impressively, they claim to get almost all of these results in one prompt, taking on average ~3 hours of thinking compute on ChatGPT Pro. Their recent result on the Navier-Stokes equations used 10,000 AI agents.

Mathematician at Anthropic Levent Alpgge calls this "obviously the most significant moment in mathematical history":

They also talk about how devastating this is for young mathematicians who were hoping to make a career solving these problems. The same mathematician says that high school students are asking him "is there anything left for me to do in mathematics".

Soon AI will be spitting out new math faster than people can read it.
